ledger.note: c. 3000 BCE: the Ahar-Banas culture settles the Banas and Berach valleys of Mewar. Infobox 'c. 3000 - c. 1500 BCE'; the culture 'lasting from c. 3000 to 1500 BCE, contemporary and adjacent to the Indus Valley civilization'; 'More than 90 sites of the Ahar culture have been identified'. The year is the infobox's; the country is the page's rivers and districts.

ledger.note: c. 1600 BCE: the Malwa plateau passes to the Malwa culture. The Malwa page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa_culture) says it was 'mainly dated to c. 1600 - c. 1300 BCE' and 'preceded by the Kayatha, Ahar-Banas, and Savalda cultures'; the Ahar page lists Jawad, Mandsaur, Kayatha and Dangwada in Madhya Pradesh. No page dates the handover; -1600 is Malwa's start (its radiocarbon dates reach back to c. 2000-1750).

notes: Type culture although the schema describes cultures before 3400 BCE: the Indus dossier (sa-01-a) uses the same convention. The page gives no area (so no sanity check is possible; there is no Cliopatria row), no phase breakdown and no account of the end. Shapes: Banswara and Dungarpur are not gazetteer places (a 50 km disc at 74.2E 23.7N stands in); Jaipur 100 km and Alwar 60 km are subtracted because the Ochre Coloured Pottery dossier (this batch) draws them from -2000, which clips a sliver of the Tonk district from -3000. The Malwa handover in -1600 is bridging (confidence 1): the Malwa page's own beginning is 'mainly c. 1600', with calibrated dates 'as early as c. 2000-1750', and the Ahar page does not mention Malwa. The Gilund seal cache (2100-1700 BC) is dated but is not a territorial event. Black and red ware (the infobox successor) is a pottery tradition on a page without infobox or extent (listed in sources); no dossier was written for it.
